pairs.subject: translation-pipeline-topology
pairs.evidence: i18n/locales.ts:5 The registry claims a new locale is a one-line edit. In fact the Python side keeps its own independent list (pipeline/jobfit/i18n.py:25 LANG_NAMES, synced only by a comment, plus role_research_cli.py:90 LANGS). So adding a language means editing several language lists, which fails the one-line-diff test.

techniques.evidence: i18n/locales.ts:6 The TS registry is the single source inside the Next app: the type, the guard and the switcher all derive from it. The Python prompt-language list and several CLI LANGS tuples re-declare it with no derivation and no pin. The one TS copy that is pinned is reasoning-cache-policy.ts:48, which a test ties to this file.

i18n/server.ts:14 Resolution goes cookie, then Accept-Language, then canonical en. setLocale (actions.ts:59) refuses to write any locale without a catalog, so nothing can be offered that is not served. Per-key fallback is not needed because the parity gate keeps catalogs complete.

pairs.evidence: scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:75 The review lenses judge commit intent, scope and constitution rules over diffs. Their only touch with localization is noting that the locale-parity gate already ran (here) and listing scripts/i18n-check.mjs as a protected path (constitution-check.mjs:197). A search of scripts/review found no translation, termbase, glossary or pseudo-locale construct, so no catalog storage, movement or translation request lives in this context.
